Definition: to rend, i.e. open (especially the mouth)
BiblicalUsage: Patsah means to open wide, to rend, especially the mouth. The earth opens her mouth to receive Abel's blood in Genesis 4:11, and Jephthah says in Judges 11:35 that he has opened his mouth unto the Lord and cannot go back. God tells Ezekiel in Ezekiel 2:8 to open his mouth and eat what He gives him, and in Lamentations 2:16 the enemies open their mouth wide against Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the opened mouth is the Bible's test of the heart: Abel's blood cries from the ground, Jephthah's vow cannot be taken back, Ezekiel eats the word, and the enemy's mouth is opened in scorn. My position is that what I open my mouth to say is what I will have to live with.
RelatedPeople: Cain; Jephthah, Judge of Israel; Ezekiel
